shared:action.description: Canonical navigation target object (Action['type']/['value']/['params'], src/lib/page-tree/action.ts). The single shared definition referenced via `{type: 'object', shape: 'action'}` by kind:button.core.action, kind:content-card.core.action, and kind:image.core.action — one Action shape, three consumers (MIO-3926).

value.description: Canonical value — no scheme/# prefix. Meaning depends on `type` (bare email address, bare anchor id, full URL, system-page-type/UUID/path, or playlist id).

params.description: Optional string-keyed query params merged onto the resolved href.

shared:background.description: Flattened TemplateSurface Background discriminated union (src/lib/page-tree/types.ts). Validation limitation: enum applies to `type`; all variant fields are optional and the validator cannot enforce which fields are required per `type` value. `thumbnail` is excluded per the honesty policy (decision 4) — declared as a TODO in hub types, implemented nowhere, used by no recipe.

type.description: Discriminant. `none` = no override (most common). `color` = theme token (see `token`). `custom-color` = explicit hex (see `value`). `tint` = themed secondary tint band, no extra fields. `image` = image URL (see `url`/`blur`/`scrim`); the renderer composes a secondary-tint scrim over the image by default (MIO-492 amendment) — `scrim:false` opts out (MIO-3134). `gradient` = resolves via the sibling `gradient` setting on the same surface. `gradient-glow` = page fill + one wide accent radial-gradient ellipse rising from the top edge, masked to fade before the bottom 40% (DS hub-section-bg.tsx gradient-glow parity; `swap` not ported). `gradient-tint` = opaque page fill + one overlay linear-gradient at a fixed 20% color-mix strength, resolved via the same resolveGradientStops() the `gradient` type consults, with the second stop hue/lightness-boosted after resolution (boostGradientTintEndStop()) so close-together schemes don't read as imperceptible once mixed down.

token.description: Used when type='color'. Theme token name, resolved via BG_TOKEN_CLASS (node-surface.tsx) to a Tailwind bg-* class. An unrecognized token renders no background (dev console.warn). 'white' = a white fill (bg-white); a band painted white reads as light for the surface auto-contrast. On kind:button a white fill takes the brand-secondary colour for its label, never primary (see kind:button.textTheme). Sections may use it too.

value.description: Used when type='custom-color'. Explicit hex value (e.g. '#FF5722'), validated via hexToRgb before use.

url.description: Used when type='image'. Validated same-origin-relative or absolute http(s) URL; CSS-delimiter characters are rejected (isValidImageUrl, node-surface.tsx). An invalid URL renders no image layer.

blur.description: Used when type='image'. Opt-in additional 25px backdrop blur layer, decoupled from `scrim` (MIO-3134/MIO-3335) — legal in every scrim on/off combination, not force-disabled by `scrim:false`.

scrim.description: Used when type='image'. MIO-3134: opt OUT of the always-on secondary-tint scrim — false renders the raw image with no darkening layer at all. Default (unset/true) is byte-identical to pre-MIO-3134 (scrim always composes, MIO-492 amendment). Pairs with shared:surface.ink — with the scrim off there is no scrimmed-image contrast to auto-derive, so the manual ink escape hatch is how the author takes over ('turn off the scrim, you own the ink').

tone.description: Used when type='tint'. 'primary' (MIO-2896) is the brand-tinted wash — the composite bg-hub-primary-bg token at node tier; at section tier (no opaque primary-family class exists) it routes to a two-layer composite (opaque bg-background fill + flat bg-hub-primary-bg overlay) instead of falling back to neutral's class.

fade.description: Used when type='tint'. Unset = flat fill. 'down' renders the same tone colour as a top-to-bottom gradient into transparent (3-stop curve: boosted top stop → floor at 40% → hold).

glowTint.description: Used when type='gradient-glow'. Tints the radial ellipse with the theme's accent colour.

glowStrength.description: Used when type='gradient-glow'. Ellipse opacity/intensity step.

glowSpread.description: Used when type='gradient-glow'. Ellipse radius step.

shared:gradient.description: Paired with shared:background when type='gradient' (src/lib/page-tree/types.ts Gradient, src/lib/theme/types.ts GradientType).

type.description: When not 'custom', resolves against the hub theme's primary color via computeGradient(). When 'custom', customStart/customEnd are used directly. Editor labels (the catalog schema has no per-enum-value label field, so the friendly names live here), in this fixed display order: split 'Balanced Blend', complementary 'Color Opposites', analogous 'Similar Shades', triadic 'Three-Way Mix', monochrome 'Single Hue', warm-shift 'Warm Glow', custom 'Custom'. The ids and their colour math are unchanged.

customStart.description: Used when type='custom'. Hex start stop, validated via hexToRgb. An invalid/missing pair falls back to 'split' against the hub theme.

customEnd.description: Used when type='custom'. Hex end stop, validated via hexToRgb.

shared:textTheme.description: Text theme — the ONE ink a whole node is painted (the hub editor's Text theme control: Auto / Dark / Light / Primary / Custom). Referenced as a `textTheme` settings key via `{type: 'object', shape: 'textTheme'}` by kind:text and kind:headline (the whole node's copy), kind:button (the label and icon ink) and kind:divider (the line's colour); its keys nest under that field on the node (`settings.textTheme.tone`, `settings.textTheme.color`). Unset — the `textTheme` key absent, or an object with no `tone` — is Auto: the consumer's own default decides (text/headline: the surrounding surface's ink, per the MIO-492 auto-contrast / `surface.ink`; button: derived from its fill; divider: the current colour). Each consumer's own field description states its Auto.

tone.description: Unset = Auto (see the shape description). 'primary' paints the hub's primary brand colour. 'secondary' paints the hub's secondary brand colour (its ink — the editor's 'Dark' option), even on a dark band. 'white' paints white (the editor's 'Light' option), even on a light band. 'custom' paints the sibling `color`; a missing or invalid `color` falls back to Auto.

color.description: Custom colour as a hex string `#rrggbb` (a 3-digit `#rgb` is also accepted). Only read when `tone` is 'custom'; ignored otherwise. Any other value is ignored by the renderer (no error), which then falls back to Auto.

shared:visibility.description: Per-viewport responsive show/hide (MIO-4182). Promoted into its own referenceable shape out of what used to be `shared:surface.visibility`'s inline properties, so the SAME {mobile, desktop} vocabulary is reachable two ways with zero drift risk between them: nested under a `surface` settings group (`shared:surface.visibility`, back-compat — see that key's own description) and as the generic top-level `visibility` settings key every node kind can carry regardless of whether it has a `surface` group at all (`shared:structural.visibility`, the new MIO-4182 path). Both reference THIS ONE definition via `{type:'object', shape:'visibility'}` — a stored value means exactly the same thing under either path.

mobile.description: false hides on max-md (Tailwind max-md:hidden). Unset/true = visible.

desktop.description: false hides on md+ (Tailwind md:hidden). Unset/true = visible.

shared:surface.description: TemplateSurface (src/lib/page-tree/types.ts). Nested under a kind's own `surface` settings key (see kind:stack, kind:content-card, and the section-root template-level surface consumed via TemplateSurface). Resolved by useNodeSurface() (src/components/primitives/node-surface.tsx).

gradient.description: See shared:gradient. Only consulted when background.type='gradient'.

padding.description: Named spacing token (PADDING_CLASS, node-surface.tsx) OR a raw CSS escape-hatch string (e.g. '15px', '1.25rem') — freeform:true means the enum lists the KNOWN named tokens but any other string value is also legal (rendered as an inline style), not a validation error. 'section' contributes VERTICAL inset only (py-hub-section) and is only visually complete on a maxWidth:'content' container root (see kind:container.maxWidth). 'gutter' = px-hub-section-x alone (X-only named step, for a surface whose vertical padding is a custom freeform value that can't merge with a named step). 'gutter-b-mobile' = mobile-only pb-4. 'hero-mobile-insets' = combined pt-16/pb-4 mobile pair. 'card' = the DS card padding pair (p-7, @max-[659px]/hub:p-4). 'band' = the standard sales section band rhythm (py-[80px], @max-[659px]/hub:py-[48px]). 'band-b' = bottom-only band variant (pb-[80px], @max-[659px]/hub:pb-[48px]). 'band-carousel' = the tighter carousel band rhythm (py-[56px], @max-[659px]/hub:py-[40px]). 'band-wave' = the wave-notch band (pt-[112px] pb-[128px], @max-[659px]/hub:pt-[80px] @max-[659px]/hub:pb-[96px]). 'card-md' = the 32px/24px card pair (p-8, @max-[659px]/hub:p-6), distinct from 'md' (p-8 flat, unchanged at mobile).

borderRadius.description: Named radius token (RADIUS_CLASS, node-surface.tsx) OR a raw CSS escape-hatch string (e.g. '12px', '50%') — freeform:true, same semantics as padding above.

shadow.description: Named shadow token (SHADOW_CLASS, node-surface.tsx). NO raw-CSS escape hatch (legacy parity, discrete sizes only) — unlike padding/borderRadius, an unrecognized value is NOT a freeform fallback, it resolves to no shadow class.

visibility.description: Responsive show/hide, nested under this surface group — see shared:visibility for the referenced {mobile, desktop} shape. Historically section-root-only (TemplateSurface applies it directly); useNodeSurface() (the resolver shared by non-section-root surfaces like stack/content-card) folds it into its returned `className` UNCONDITIONALLY, so any consumer that applies that resolved className to its DOM node picks it up automatically — today that's kind:stack's own `surface` (see kind:stack.presentational.surface) and the generic (non-hub_playlists) kind:content-card card body (see kind:content-card.presentational.surface). The one exception is the delegated HubPlaylistCard path inside content-card (hub_playlists scope), which supplies its own chrome and never applies the resolved surface className/style at all — nested `surface.visibility` has no render effect there. PRESERVED FOR BACK-COMPAT (MIO-4182): an existing stored tree's `surface.visibility` keeps meaning exactly what it always meant. New authoring that needs visibility on a kind with no `surface` group — or wants one consistent path regardless of kind — should prefer the generic top-level `visibility` key (shared:structural.visibility, MIO-4182) instead; this nested key is not deprecated, just no longer the only path.

minHeight.description: Section-root-only concern (like visibility). Literal whitelist, NO raw-CSS escape hatch — a fixed DS design token, not free-form author input (MIN_HEIGHT_CLASS, template-surface.tsx). 500 = unconditional min-h-[500px] (search-bar band). 440 = @[660px]/hub:min-h-[440px], gated to >=660px container width (testimonials carousel band, MIO-2678) — mobile takes natural height.

margin.description: Freeform raw-CSS escape hatch (e.g. '-40px 0 0'), no named-token form. Lets a node escape its own box — padding can only add inset space. NOT authorable via any admin content field; this is a template-recipe-level layout escape hatch (straddle/edge authoring contracts), not a writable author knob.

translate.description: Freeform raw-CSS escape hatch (e.g. '0 -50%') mapped to the CSS `translate` property. Own-box-relative percentages (unlike vertical margin %, which resolves against containing-block width) — the vocabulary's only 'shift by half MY OWN height' mechanism. Composes with rotate/scale in the fixed CSS individual-transform-property order. Recipe-authoring-level escape hatch, not a writable author knob.

clip.description: Opt-in overflow-hidden clipping the surface's own in-flow children to its borderRadius — independent of the pre-existing backgroundLayer clip gate.

elevate.description: Opt-in relative z-10 giving the surface's own box paint-order priority over a neighboring section that is independently position:relative (e.g. via its own layered background). Required whenever `edge` or a margin+translate straddle overlaps a positioned neighbor.

edge.description: A repeating shape-tile mask cut into the surface's own top/bottom edge, painted with the surface's own resolved background. AUTHORING CONTRACT: setting edge.top/bottom:'wave' requires ALSO setting, on the SAME surface: (1) `margin` — negative offset on that side equal to the 32px tile height; (2) `padding` on that same side increased by the same 32px; (3) `elevate:true`. None of the three are auto-computed — omitting any renders a clipped/misaligned/wrongly-stacked strip.

minScreenHeight.description: dvh (not vh, for mobile chrome collapse). Pairs with flex flex-col — does not force centering itself. WINS over `minHeight` when both are set (minHeight's resolution is skipped entirely, not merged).

maxHeight.description: px, static class-map ladder, no freeform. Independent of minHeight/minScreenHeight.

ink.description: MIO-3134: manual override of the resolved auto-contrast ink (--foreground/--muted-foreground/--muted trio, MIO-492) — general across EVERY background variant, not image-scoped. 'auto' (default) keeps today's per-background derivation, including 'no remap' for variants that don't derive one (tint, gradient-glow, gradient-tint, none). 'light' forces pure white ink; 'dark' forces the theme's brand-secondary ink — the same two poles resolveSurfaceContrast()'s own derivation already picks between (surface-contrast.ts), and the same two-way choice the MIO-3224 on-primary ink policy makes. Non-string/unrecognized values are tolerated as 'auto' (never throws).

shared:structural.description: NOT referenced via {type:'object',shape:'structural'} from a kind descriptor like the other shared shapes. This is a validator-level ADDITIVE allowlist: every node's settings object is validated against `kind:<its-kind>` UNIONED with these three keys — tab_label/slot are read generically off ANY child node's settings by an ANCESTOR container (tabs.tsx, accordion.tsx, find-by-slot.ts), independent of the child's own kind, and are not part of any single kind's own *Settings TS interface; surface is read generically off ANY node's settings by renderer.tsx's <TemplateSurface> wrapper, gated on that node's `template` annotation naming a templates[]/pageTemplates[] entry that itself declares a `surface` property (the surface-declaring template set), independent of the node's own kind. This is an extension beyond the design spec's literal decision-1 text (which only names shared:surface as a referenced shape); documented here because the real catalog already uses tab_label/slot on stack/text/tabs nodes and surface on section-root container nodes (see Task A1 defaults-audit notes + MIO-2685 review round 1), and excluding any of the three would make the validator reject existing recipes. MIO-2724 addendum: `name`/`role`/`salesMeta` (REVIEW — flagged for owner confirmation, see their own descriptions) extend this additive allowlist with catalog-authoring-only narrative-arc metadata used by the page-sales recipe's section-root nodes — distinct from any mio-hub renderer concern, and (for `role`) a deliberate same-name/different-vocabulary overload against kind:field.core.role, resolved safely by this validator's kind-first-then-structural-fallback lookup order. MIO-3134/MIO-3278 addendum: `side`/`logoSize` are region-chrome settings read off the ROOT of mio-hub's auth brand-panel tree slot (src/lib/auth/prepare-panel-region.ts) by that ONE bespoke consumer — not by NodeRenderer/useNodeSurface and not generic across every node the way tab_label/slot are. Gated the SAME way `surface` is: legal only when the node's own `template` annotation names a member of the regionChrome-declaring template set (a templates[]/pageTemplates[] entry carrying a top-level `regionChrome` property, e.g. `auth-brand-panel`) — an ungated placement would let any stray node author side/logoSize with no consumer ever reading them there. MIO-4182 addendum: `visibility` extends this additive allowlist with an UNCONDITIONAL per-viewport show/hide key (shared:visibility shape) — unconditional like tab_label/slot, NOT gated like surface/side/logoSize, so it validates on every node kind regardless of `template`. It is a NEW top-level path onto the exact same {mobile, desktop} vocabulary `shared:surface.visibility` has always carried; see both keys' own descriptions for the back-compat/precedence story. Status honesty (MIO-2584): this vocabulary addition documents only what the mio-hub renderer implements in the SAME change set it ships with — see the PR description for the exact landing commit.

tab_label.description: Read by tabs.tsx and accordion.tsx off a DIRECT CHILD's own settings (getLabel()) to label that child's tab/accordion trigger — independent of the child's own kind. Falls back to 'Tab N' / index-based label when absent or non-string.

slot.description: Read by find-by-slot.ts (src/lib/page-tree/data-binding/find-by-slot.ts) to locate a node by a named slot, for patch/cascade addressing — independent of the node's own kind.

visibility.description: MIO-4182 — per-viewport responsive show/hide, read generically off ANY node's settings at the TOP level (`settings.visibility`, a sibling of `settings.surface` and every other kind-specific settings key) — UNCONDITIONAL, same unconditional additive path as tab_label/slot above, unlike `surface`'s gated-by-template path below. Same shape/values as the surface group's own `visibility` (shared:visibility) — a leaf kind with no `surface` settings key at all (e.g. headline, button, image) can still set `settings.visibility` directly, and a container kind that already has its own `surface` group (stack, content-card) can use this instead of nesting. `surface.visibility` (shared:surface.visibility) is NOT deprecated by this — it is the pre-existing back-compat path for the kinds/templates that already honour it there (TemplateSurface section roots, kind:stack); this key extends the SAME semantics to every kind via one consistent top-level location. A node that sets BOTH this key and a nested `surface.visibility` is not a conflict this catalog arbitrates — authors should set one, not both; the consuming renderer decides precedence if both are present.

surface.description: Read generically off ANY node's settings by renderer.tsx's <TemplateSurface> wrapper (renderer.tsx:150-162), gated on node.template being in the surface-declaring template set, independent of the node's own kind. Kinds that ALSO read it at the node tint tier declare it themselves (kind:stack, kind:content-card).

side.description: MIO-3134/MIO-3278 — region-chrome setting on the ROOT of a regionChrome-gated template (see the shared:structural top-level description). Which side of the split-screen mio-hub's auth brand-panel renders on. Read tolerantly by the one bespoke consumer (prepare-panel-region.ts's parseSide) — any value other than 'left' resolves to 'right', its default when unset.

logoSize.description: MIO-3134/MIO-3227/MIO-3335/MIO-3278 — region-chrome setting, same regionChrome gate as `side` above. 'normal' (unset default) is today's fixed-logo chrome sizing; 'hero' is a larger tier mirroring kind:logo's own 'hero' height step. ALSO accepts an absolute px NUMBER — freeform:true admits any number here; the consumer (prepare-panel-region.ts's parseLogoSize) clamps it to [16,320] and falls back to 'normal' outside that range or for any other unrecognized value, the same [16,320] range kind:logo.height's own numeric escape uses.

name.description: REVIEW: catalog-authoring-only narrative section slug (e.g. "the-struggle") — generic across kinds via the same additive fallback as slot/tab_label. Not consumed by the mio-hub renderer. See the shared:structural top-level description for the full name-collision + scope note.

role.description: REVIEW: catalog-authoring-only narrative-arc role tag (which beat of the sales-page arc this section plays). Distinct vocabulary from kind:field.core.role — see the shared:structural top-level description.

section.description: Section number in reading order. Fractional values (e.g. 10.5) mark a section inserted between two originally-numbered ones.

shape.description: Which narrative-beat template this section follows.

compactGroup.description: Optional pairing key grouping sections that share one compact-layout treatment. null = ungrouped.

prompt.description: Authoring-time reminder of what content this section's copy should say. Never rendered.

salesMeta.description: REVIEW: catalog-authoring-only per-section narrative metadata block, sibling of `name`/`role`/`slot`. Not consumed by the mio-hub renderer — pure recipe-authoring documentation. See the shared:structural top-level description for the full rationale and the owner-review flag.

width.description: Row/columns unification (MIO-2137): makes this stack behave as a responsive COLUMN inside a `row` — full-width on mobile, its flex-grow ratio at/above the hub 660px container-query breakpoint. Requires an ancestor declaring @container/hub. "fit" is a DIFFERENT mechanism from the row-column members — a shrink-wrap (w-fit), for pairing a button with e.g. a doodle{variant:"underline"} at the button's own edge width.

surface.description: Column-level visual surface (MIO-2335) — same TemplateSurface vocabulary as section roots, at the 'node' tint tier. CORRECTION (MIO-4182): `visibility` IS honoured here — mio-hub's useNodeSurface() (node-surface.tsx) folds `surface.visibility` into this stack's own resolved classes exactly like TemplateSurface does for a section root, independent of `template`. (The generic kind:content-card card body resolves it the same way — see kind:content-card.presentational.surface; mio-hub's editor-only `honoursVisibility()`, src/lib/editor/canvas-node-category.ts, gates the canvas hide-chip affordance, not renderer support, and is not evidence either way here.) A prior revision of this description claimed the opposite ('NOT honoured here, section-root-only') — that was stale/wrong, not a renderer change; see shared:surface.visibility.

mobileGap.description: Opt-in mobile-narrower gap step (DS playlist header content column).

grow.description: Opt-in min-w-0 flex-1 so this stack fills the remaining width of a plain flex row beside a fixed-size sibling.

justify.description: Main-axis (vertical) distribution, mirroring row.justify. No "around" member.

fitMobile.description: Drops the `width:"fit"` full-width-on-mobile flip (pairs with dropping the paired button's own fullWidthMobile — the two move together).

hideOnMobile.description: Literal @max-[659px]/hub:hidden on the whole stack — hides the subtree below the hub container's 660px breakpoint.

gap.description: Flex-row gap step, plus the 'section' sentinel (gap-hub-section-gap, row.tsx:92) — matches RowSettings.gap's mixed union; under the enum-subsumes-type rule the type field is not load-bearing here.

responsive.description: Opt-in DS responsive-intent row: stacks below the container's 660px, becomes a row (vertically centered) at/above it. Requires an ancestor declaring @container/hub.

split.description: Opt-in [&>*]:flex-1 [&>*]:min-w-0 so direct children divide the row evenly (DS 50/50 split).

wrap.description: Opt-in flex-wrap, used by the unified `row` section's body so 1-4 column stack children wrap.

fullWidth.description: Opt-in w-full so the row fills its parent's width even inside an items-start flex column.

maxWidth.description: Opt-in max-width cap (DS playlist header sections).

reverse.description: Opt-in desktop-only visual-order reverse (@[660px]/hub:flex-row-reverse). Mobile/stacked state unaffected.

alignMobile.description: Cross-axis alignment override applied only below the hub container's 660px breakpoint.

variant.description: Layout variant. 'legacy' = flat grid with configurable cols/gap (default). 'ds-content' = DS-aligned content-page grid with its own section band + containment. 'responsive' = DS grid-section column progression (1->3@660->4@1024) WITHOUT its own section band — relies on an ancestor's TemplateSurface for the @container/hub context.

slidesPerView.description: Slides visible per view (drives static SLIDE_BASIS flex-basis classes; the primitive supports 1-4 with static Tailwind classes).

interval_ms.description: Autoplay interval in milliseconds. Only meaningful when autoplay=true.

bleed.description: MIO-2678 full-bleed opt-in — the viewport spans the full section width; each slide's content and the controls row carry the section gutter internally instead of a wrapping container.

effect.description: 'blur-fade': one slide per grid cell, 400ms fade+blur+translate, banked-pause autoplay. 'marquee': continuously drifting strip via real scrollLeft, pauses on hover/focus/touch/reduced-motion, ignores `bleed`. Both bypass Embla; a `quote` child auto-switches to the DS grid-card presentation.

itemWidth.description: 'card' fixes each item wrapper to a DS card width (~300px, the `compact` scroll recipe). 'auto' (default) leaves sizing to the child's own layout.

kind:tabs._note: The Tabs component reads NO settings of its own (PRIMITIVE_DEFAULTS explicitly documents this: "tabs — the component reads no settings at all"). Its per-child tab label comes from shared:structural's tab_label on each CHILD's own settings, not from a tabs-kind setting.

kind:container._note: No PRIMITIVE_DEFAULTS entry (container: {}) — the DS-intended maxWidth:'content' default has NO inline `??` fallback in container.tsx, deliberately undeclared per that file's own comment (would change rendering the moment MIO-2358 wires cascade layer 1).

background.description: Simple background token — UNRELATED to shared:background/TemplateSurface; this is container.tsx's own small enum.

maxWidth.description: Content-width cap + gutter. 'content' is the DS gutter-outside-cap idiom (MIO-2128) that pairs with shared:surface.padding='section' on an ancestor surface.

actionFromScope.description: Names a scope key (a data-source-injected Action object) that becomes this card's stretched-link navigation target when the content-node/playlist-target-derived href doesn't resolve.

action.description: Static fallback navigation target for this card's stretched link — the shared kind:button Action shape (type/value/params). Priority order (same fallback direction kind:button already uses — dynamic/bound beats static): the bound content-node/playlist-target-derived href wins first, then `actionFromScope` when it resolves to a valid Action, then this static `action` as the last resort.

surface.description: Generic-card-body visual surface (MIO-2335), 'node' tint tier, applied to the outer role=group wrapper. Only affects the generic (NodeRenderer) card body — NOT the delegated HubPlaylistCard path (hub_playlists scope), which supplies its own chrome. CORRECTION (MIO-4182): nested `visibility` IS honoured for the generic card body — content-card.tsx (src/components/primitives/containers/content-card.tsx) resolves this surface through the SAME useNodeSurface() kind:stack uses, and that hook unconditionally folds `surface.visibility` into its returned `className` (node-surface.tsx); content-card applies that className whenever `applySurface` (`!isPlaylistCard`) is true, which is every generic (non-hub_playlists) card. The ONE true exception is the delegated HubPlaylistCard path (hub_playlists scope): it supplies its own card chrome and never applies the resolved surface className/style at all, so a nested `surface.visibility` set there has no render effect. A prior revision of this description claimed the opposite for content-card as a whole ('NOT currently read by content-card's renderer') — that was stale/wrong, and wrongly cited mio-hub's editor-only `honoursVisibility()` (src/lib/editor/canvas-node-category.ts, gates the canvas hide-chip affordance) as if it were renderer evidence; it isn't — see shared:surface.visibility. A hub_playlists card — or any node whose kind has no `surface` settings key at all — that needs show/hide should use the generic top-level `visibility` key (shared:structural.visibility) instead.

newTab.description: Opens the resolved href in a new tab.

embed_type.description: 'native' renders an HTML5 <video>; 'iframe' renders a sandboxed <iframe> gated through isAllowedEmbedUrl (an unlisted host renders an inline error, not the iframe).

fileId.description: File id to load (alternative binding path to `value`). When set, the video element plays that hub library file through the hub player (poster from the file, HLS, progress tracking) instead of the `value` URL. `fileId` wins over `value` when both are set.

maxWidth.description: Per-node MAX-width cap in px for the video box, centred in its column. Same clamp/behaviour contract as kind:image's maxWidth (MIO-4112): the renderer clamps it to [16, 1440] and applies it via inline `max-width`; it is always a MAX, so the video fills its column up to the cap and shrinks below it on narrow viewports. No enum presets here — kind:image's 352/128 members are DS-measured image-specific caps that don't apply to video; this is a plain freeform number, same shape as kind:media-slot's `width`.

radius.description: The player frame's corner radius — same contract as kind:image's radius (ui/thumbnail `radius`): 'control' (0.5× hub radius), 'control-l' (0.6×, the default the hub renderer applies), 'm' (1× hub radius). Presets follow the hub-wide corner-radius setting. ALSO accepts an absolute px NUMBER (MIO-4112) — freeform:true admits any number here; the renderer clamps it to [0,200] and applies it via inline `border-radius`, so it deliberately does NOT follow the hub radius. 0 = square corners. A per-video number overrides the hub-wide radius for that video only. Any other unrecognized value falls back to 'control-l'.

poster.description: Custom thumbnail shown before playback, overriding the library file's own thumbnail (fileId) or standing in for a direct video URL (value). A durable hub image URL, validated like image sources (isValidImageUrl). Unset: a library file shows its own thumbnail; a direct URL shows the first frame; an embedded provider (YouTube, Vimeo) shows its own and ignores this.

variant.description: 'wave' — a drawn rule tiling at a fixed amplitude.

weight.description: Stroke thickness, clamped [0.5,24]. No hard default — computed (1 for line, size-derived for wave) when unset.

inset.description: Percent, clamped [0,50]. Shortens the rule from each end.

dashed.description: Renders the rule dashed instead of solid. Applies to variant 'line'; ignored by 'wave'.

textTheme.description: See shared:textTheme. The line's colour, still drawn at `opacity`. Unset = Auto: the current colour (the surrounding ink), exactly as without the key.

valueFrom.description: Names a scope key holding a numeric 0-100 progress value (MIO-2248); takes priority over the static `value` when the scope value coerces to a finite number.

label.description: Accessible name for the progressbar role. Defaults to 'Progress'.

size.description: Pixel diameter. DS ring sizes are 16 | 24 | 48 | 64 | 76, but the underlying type is an unconstrained number (ui/progress accepts any value) — not a hard enum.

mobileSize.description: Opt-in mobile pixel diameter — when set, renders TWO ring hosts that container-query-swap (>=660px shows `size`, <660px shows `mobileSize`), matching the DS's dual-ring pattern rather than one ring that resizes.

variant.description: Surface variant. 'default' = light. 'white' = for dark/colourful surfaces.

level.description: Heading level 1-6, drives both the rendered tag and the DS type-scale size mapping (SIZE_BY_LEVEL).

weight.description: Font weight. MIO-985 Thread B: default headlines are font-normal (400), not the old font-semibold.

highlight.description: Phrase(s) to emphasise — accent colour, no wash by default. Case-sensitive literal substring, every occurrence flagged.

highlightUnderline.description: Underlines HIGHLIGHTED runs only. No-op without `highlight`.

size.description: Opt-in DISPLAY-size override — `level` still owns semantics (heading tag, one-h1-dedupe). Landing/sales-page only — no hub PAGE should reach for large-title/xl-title.

alignMobile.description: Text-alignment override applied only below the hub container's 660px breakpoint.

format.description: Opt-in interpretation of `value`. `plain` (default) renders `value` verbatim as plain text — existing trees are unaffected. `markdown` renders `value` on ONE line inside the heading element: bold/italic/underline/strikethrough/highlight and links render as inline marks (**bold**, _italic_, ++underline++, ~~strikethrough~~, ==highlight==; the highlight wears the same wash as kind:text's); paragraphs, lists, headings, blockquotes, code and tables render as inline text — their words are kept, the block structure is dropped, and separate blocks (and hard line breaks) join with a space. Horizontal rules and images never render; an inline HTML tag is stripped but its text is kept, an HTML block is removed along with its content. Only absolute http(s)/mailto:/tel: links and /, #, ?-prefixed relative links become anchors — anything else (e.g. www.example.com, a bare relative path, //host, sms:) renders as plain text. `highlight` (with `highlightUnderline`/`highlightStyle`) still applies on top of the markdown output, per plain-text run: a phrase that crosses a mark boundary does not match. The hub editor writes `markdown` on the first inline edit of a headline that is not inside a data-bound subtree (an ancestor, or the node itself, carrying `dataSource`/`repeat`); a headline inside one is edited as plain text.

textTheme.description: See shared:textTheme. The Text theme — the one colour the WHOLE heading is painted; unset = Auto (the surrounding section surface's own ink, per the MIO-492 auto-contrast / `surface.ink`, exactly as without the key). Same semantics as kind:text.textTheme. `highlight` runs and inline marks keep their own treatment ('accent' runs stay the primary colour; a wash keeps full ink over its wash).

size.description: 2-size DS scale (MIO-985 Thread B). "body-big" is a third opt-in step for callout/bridge lines; no responsive container-query shrink (unlike body/small).

clamp.description: Opt-in line clamp (DS HubDescription maxLines). Unconstrained number type, but only small integers 1-6 are honoured — any other value is defensively ignored by the renderer (no error, silent no-op), not enforced as a hard enum.

muted.description: Opt-in muted-text override (text-foreground/75). Only applies on the non-clamped render path — the clamped path already renders muted unconditionally. Still honoured by the renderer, but no longer offered in the hub editor's appearance popover (Text theme / `textTheme` is the only colour control there). A set `textTheme.tone` wins over it.

tone.description: Legacy opt-in colour tone, kept for back-compat — the shipped eyebrow recipes and older trees carry it. 'primary' applies text-primary and wins over `muted` when both are set. Superseded by `textTheme`: new authoring writes `textTheme` instead, and a set `textTheme.tone` wins over this key.

textTheme.description: See shared:textTheme. The Text theme — the one colour the WHOLE node's copy is painted; unset = Auto (the surrounding section surface's own ink, per the MIO-492 auto-contrast / `surface.ink`, exactly as without the key). A set `textTheme.tone` wins over `muted` and the legacy `tone`, applies on the clamped render path too (replacing its default 75% ink), and with `variant: 'eyebrow'` replaces only the eyebrow's colour while with `variant: 'bullet'` it paints the whole row (glyph and hairline follow the row's ink). Inline marks (e.g. a `==highlight==` wash) keep their own treatment.

highlight.description: Search-highlight wash. Mutually exclusive with `clamp` (clamp wins).

variant.description: Opt-in bundle, wins over size/weight/color. 'eyebrow' — uppercase, letter-spaced label above a headline. 'bullet' — a DS list-item row (glyph + top hairline, MIO-3314). No effect on the clamped render path.

alignMobile.description: Text-alignment override applied only below the hub container's 660px breakpoint.

format.description: Opt-in interpretation of `value`. `plain` (default) renders `value` verbatim as plain text — existing trees are unaffected. `markdown` renders `value` as a restricted markdown subset: paragraphs (blank line), hard line breaks, **bold**, _italic_, links, bullet and ordered lists, and horizontal rules. Headings, blockquotes, and code (inline, fenced, and indented) render as plain paragraphs or inline text, never their own elements. `~~strikethrough~~` (or `~single~` tildes), `++underline++` and `==highlight==` render as inline marks (a backslash-escaped marker such as `C\+\+` stays literal); table syntax renders as literal text; an inline HTML tag is stripped but its text is kept, an HTML block is removed along with its content; images never render. Only absolute http(s)/mailto:/tel: links and /, #, ?-prefixed relative links become anchors — anything else (e.g. www.example.com, a bare relative path, //host, sms:) renders as plain text. Markdown formatting applies on every non-clamped node regardless of whether `highlight` or a `variant` bundle is set on the same node; a clamped node (`clamp` set) renders this markdown subset the same way.

kind:image._note: EXCLUDES `width`/`height` from ImageSettings — the hub interface comment states they are 'presently no-ops' (no longer forwarded to the rendered , ui/thumbnail owns that element with no sizing passthrough), kept on the TS contract only for BE-served-data forward-compat parsing, not for authoring. Per the honesty policy, a key with no rendering effect does not enter the vocabulary. Same reasoning removed `outline` (owner decision 2026-09-30, retired image hairline): image.tsx now hardcodes `outline={false}` on ui/thumbnail regardless of the setting; the TS `ImageSettings.outline?` field stays on the hub contract only as a retired, documented-ignored field for old saved trees, but the key itself no longer exists in this vocabulary. `kind:media-slot`'s own `outline` is unaffected — that renderer still applies it.

action.description: Static navigation target for a STANDALONE image only — the shared kind:button Action shape (type/value/params). Do not set this on an image nested inside a linked content-card body: the card body re-enables nested anchors, so a linked image inside a linked card would win the click and produce two competing navigation targets — put the action on the card (kind:content-card.action) instead. Mutually exclusive with `lightbox`: `action` wins at runtime when both would apply, and the catalog validator rejects a node that sets both.

aspectRatio.description: Fixed aspect preset, mapped to ui/thumbnail's `aspect` prop. '4:3' has no direct thumbnail preset — mapped to 'preview' plus an override class.

objectFit.description: 'contain' takes priority over aspectRatio and always resolves to ui/thumbnail's natural (shrink-wrap) mode.

radius.description: DS thumbnail radius preset (ui/thumbnail `radius`): 'control' (0.5× hub radius), 'control-l' (0.6×, the leaf default), 'm' (1× hub radius). Presets follow the hub-wide corner-radius setting. ALSO accepts an absolute px NUMBER (MIO-4112) — freeform:true admits any number here; the renderer (ui/thumbnail.tsx) clamps it to [0,200] and applies it via inline `border-radius`, so it deliberately does NOT follow the hub radius. 0 = square corners. A per-image number overrides the hub-wide radius for that image only. Any other unrecognized value falls back to 'control-l'.

backdrop.description: Opt-IN opaque thumbnail backdrop (MIO-288 bg-background fill under the image). Unset (the new default, owner decision 2026-09-30, was opt-out under MIO-3086) renders the thumbnail surface transparent, so intentionally transparent artwork sits on the section surface underneath. Set `true` for a picture whose transparent pixels would otherwise composite with mismatched content below it. No-op without a src (MIO-3086).

maxWidth.description: Per-node MAX-width cap in px. The two enum members are the DS-measured caps (352 = the narrative one-column sections' image sub-cap, 128 = the deliverable-card icon-box cap) and render via their max-w-* classes. ALSO accepts any other px NUMBER (MIO-4112) — freeform:true admits any number; the renderer (image.tsx) clamps it to [16, 1440] and applies it via inline `max-width`. It is always a MAX: the image fills its column up to the cap and shrinks below it on narrow viewports, so a custom value cannot break a mobile layout. alignX places the capped box (mx-auto when 'center'). Non-number values are rejected by the validator.

alignX.description: Horizontal alignment of the maxWidth-capped box within its wider cell. No-op without maxWidth.

objectPosition.description: The visible anchor of the picture when it is cropped (`objectFit: cover`) — which part of the image survives the crop, as a CSS object-position keyword pair ('top-left' = left top, etc.). The nine anchors of the editor's position picker. No effect with `objectFit: contain`, where the whole picture is shown. Unset = centre.

newTab.description: Opens the resolved href in a new tab.

href.description: @deprecated legacy alias for `action` (a bare URL string). Still read as a fallback.

actionFromScope.description: Names a scope key (a data-source-injected Action object) used INSTEAD of the static action/href when the scope value resolves to a valid Action.

labelFrom.description: Names a scope key whose STRING value replaces the static label (node.value) when present and non-empty.

planGroupId.description: Id of the plan-group whose selected plan-card priceId is appended to this button's resolved href as ?price_id=…. Resolves like plan-price groupId (exact id, else the page's sole plan-group). No-op when unset, when the group has no selection, or when the selected card carries no priceId.

variant.description: Visual style, forwarded 1:1 to ui/button's variant prop. 'ghost-primary' — same silhouette as ghost-dark, for use ON a solid bg-primary surface (adaptive text-primary-foreground instead of hardcoded text-white, design-system.md §4c). Back-compat: older trees carry `variant`, and it is still honoured while `style` and `background` are both unset. New authoring (the hub editor's button popover) writes `style` + `background` (+ `gradient` / `textTheme`) instead; once either `style` or `background` is set they describe the button's look and `variant` is ignored.

style.description: The Style axis. No default: while `style` AND `background` are both unset, the button's look is decided by the legacy `variant` field instead ('secondary' renders outlined, every other variant renders filled), for back-compat. Setting `style` explicitly always wins over `variant`, even with `background` still unset — e.g. `{variant:'secondary', style:'fill'}` switches a legacy secondary button from its outlined look to the primary fill, so an explicit `style` is never redundant with silence. 'fill' = a solid button painted by `background` (Auto when `background` is unset too). 'outline' = no fill: a bordered button whose border and label take the colour the fill would have been (the resolved `background`), unless `textTheme` sets the label ink.

background.description: See shared:background. The button's fill. A button honours only: `none` / unset = Auto (today's primary fill, with the on-primary-band inversion); `color` with `token` 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'white'; `custom-color` (`value` hex); `gradient` (resolved via the sibling `gradient`). `tint`, `image`, `gradient-glow`, `gradient-tint` and any other `token` are NOT honoured on a button — the renderer treats them as Auto.

gradient.description: See shared:gradient. Only consulted when `background.type` is 'gradient' — the same schemes and colour math as a section gradient.

textTheme.description: See shared:textTheme. The label and icon ink. Unset = Auto, decided by the button's own `style`/`background` — not one luminance rule: Fill + Auto/primary token uses the DS on-primary ink rule; Fill + white token always takes the brand-secondary ink (never primary); Fill + gradient is always white, with no luminance check. Outline has no fill to derive from, so the ink follows the resolved border colour (the token/custom colour), or the ambient surface foreground for Auto.

size.description: Leaf-facing size name, mapped to ui/button size tokens (sm->sm, md->default, lg->lg).

newTab.description: Opens the resolved href in a new tab.

icon.description: Leading icon (hub sprite name), rendered before the label.

iconRight.description: Trailing icon (hub sprite name), rendered after the label.

border.description: A line around the button, on every style (fill and outline). Unset = the style's own edge: none on Fill, the 1px ring on Outline. Set, it is drawn INSIDE the button's edge on its fill layer — it never changes the button's size or layout — and follows the button's corners (`borderRadius`) and its hover grow. On Outline it IS the ring: `width` sets the ring's thickness, including a gradient ring (cut to the same even width on every side). The hub editor's Advanced options → Border card (switch off = key unset).

width.description: Line thickness in px — whole pixels 1–16, the editor's Width slider ("A border that is on is at least 1px. Zero is what the switch is for"). Required for the border to draw: a `border` without a valid `width` renders as unset.

color.description: Line colour as a hex string `#rrggbb` (a 3-digit `#rgb` is also accepted) — the same format as shared:textTheme.color. Unset = the button's own colour: on Outline the ring keeps the colour (or gradient) `background` gives it; on Fill the line takes the hub's brand-secondary colour. Any other value is ignored by the renderer (treated as unset). On an Outline gradient ring a set colour replaces the gradient on the ring; the label keeps its own ink.

style.description: Line style. A gradient ring (Outline + gradient `background`, `color` unset) is always drawn solid — a gradient cannot be dashed.

borderRadius.description: The button's corner radius, over its size's own control radius. Same vocabulary as shared:surface.borderRadius: a named radius token OR a raw CSS escape-hatch string — one length ('12px') or the four-corner shorthand ('12px 12px 0px 0px', top-left top-right bottom-right bottom-left). Applies to the whole button — fill, ring, border and focus ring follow it. Unset = the size's own radius. The hub editor's Advanced options → Corner radius card.

shadow.description: A drop shadow under the button — the same named tiers as shared:surface.shadow, drawn with the hub's ring-less drop-shadow tokens (it adds no edge line of its own, and never alters the Outline ring or `border`). NO raw-CSS escape hatch; an unrecognized value draws no shadow. Unset / 'none' = no shadow. The hub editor's Advanced options → Drop shadow card (Small 'sm' / Medium 'md' / Large 'lg').

disabled.description: Renders a non-interactive disabled button: no Link/anchor wrapper, no action/onClick. Used for locked/drip-scheduled CTAs.

fullWidthMobile.description: Full-width, tap-friendly button below the hub 660px container-query breakpoint.

compactMobile.description: Steps the 'md' size from 40px to 36px below the hub 659px breakpoint. Scoped to size:'md' only.

size.description: Pixel size, mapped to the nearest ui/icon-valid size (12|14|16|20|24|32) via toIconSize().

sizePx.description: Icon size in px set by the editor slider, clamped [12,120]; when set it wins over size; unset → size as before.

color.description: Legacy color token. Used only when `textTheme` is unset — a set `textTheme` wins. The hub editor no longer offers this control (superseded by `textTheme`); existing stored values keep rendering exactly as before.

textTheme.description: See shared:textTheme. The icon's ink. Unset = the legacy `color` token decides (back-compat, unchanged render); an absent/default `color` too falls back to `default`'s current-foreground treatment. A set `textTheme.tone` wins over `color`.

strokeWidth.description: Opt-in stroke-width override, passed straight to ui/icon and rendered exactly as stored — no renderer clamp, unchanged behavior. The hub editor's Advanced options offers 0.5–8 in 0.5 steps and bounds new values to that range before they're stored (owner raised the cap from 0.5–5); unset preserves ui/icon's own default (1.5). A value already on disk (in or out of the current range) keeps rendering exactly as given.

name.description: Required. The scope key this field reads (scope[name]).

text.description: Optional static text rendered instead of `scope[name]` when set to a non-blank string (whitespace-only counts as unset). Unset, empty, or whitespace-only falls back to `scope[name]` — byte-identical to today's behavior. When set, the field renders even if `scope[name]` is nullish — `text` takes precedence over `optional` and the dev missing-value marker (see `kind:field.presentational.optional`). Everything else about the field is unchanged: role/size/weight/clamp styling still applies, and `actionFromScope` still resolves its link from the scope regardless of which text source is rendered. Intended for a standalone heading field, not a title field inside a content-card — the card's accessible name and hover chip still read the scope title, not this field's `text`.

role.description: Semantic role within the parent template — the cascade resolver applies role-specific defaults (e.g. title gets heading-weight styling), all overridable via the explicit settings below.

actionFromScope.description: Title hover-chevron affordance — names a scope key (an Action object) that, when valid, wraps this field's text in a Link plus a decorative hover chevron.

size.description: Explicit size override. Falls back to the role default, then 'body'.

weight.description: Explicit font-weight override. Falls back to the role default (title only), then unset.

muted.description: Explicit muted-text override (text-foreground/75). Falls back to the role default.

tone.description: Opt-in color tone. 'primary' wins over `muted` when both are set. 'default' is the explicit no-tone path — same rendered result as leaving `tone` unset.

clamp.description: Opt-in line clamp, routes through ui/expandable-text. Only integers 1-6 are honoured; other values are defensively ignored (no error).

icon.description: Opt-in leading hub sprite glyph name (DS meta-chip spec). Loosely typed string (not IconName) — an unknown name safely renders an empty <use> reference rather than crashing.

value.description: Defaults to 100 (the completed-chip shape) when omitted.

size.description: Defaults to 16 (the completed-chip shape) when omitted.

ring.description: Opt-in leading progress-ring chip (DS 'Completed' chip spec) instead of `icon`. Mutually exclusive with `icon` in practice — if both set, `ring` wins.

fade.description: Opt-in single-line horizontal fade-truncate. Ignored on the clamped render path — clamp wins if both are set.

optional.description: When `text` is unset (or blank) and the bound scope value is nullish, renders null in EVERY environment (no dev '[missing: name]' marker) — unless a non-blank `text` is set, which always renders regardless of `optional`.

name.description: Required. The scope key this slot reads (scope[name]).

preset.description: Opt-in poster preset — when set AND scope.poster_variants is a non-empty object, resolves the URL via the pickPoster fallback chain instead of reading a ready scope[name] URL.

aspectRatio.description: Same styling contract as kind:image's aspectRatio.

objectFit.description: Same styling contract as kind:image's objectFit.

radius.description: Same styling contract as kind:image's radius — presets follow the hub radius; an absolute px NUMBER 0–200 (MIO-4112) is clamped and applied inline, overriding the hub radius for this slot only.

outline.description: Opt-in shadow-hub-xs outline. Media-slot-only vocabulary (MIO-2137) — the equivalent `kind:image` key was removed for a no-op hub renderer (honesty policy); this slot's own hub renderer still applies it.

width.description: Opt-in FIXED pixel width for a small tile beside a growing flex sibling. Height derives from the existing aspectRatio class, not set separately.

progressBar.description: Opt-in in-progress watch-progress bar overlay, reading scope.progressPercent. Do NOT also set on a contentCardChild()'s media-slot (content-card.tsx already renders its own bar) — would double-render.

name.description: Required. The scope key this slot reads (scope[name]), expected shape {label, href?, action?}.

fileId.description: File id to load (alternative binding path to contentId).

playlistId.description: Playlist id context for the player's up-next/queue behavior.

attachments.description: Attachment list to render (src/lib/api/content/types.ts Attachment — an API-owned shape; items are represented opaquely here, not re-declared, since Attachment is not a page-tree settings type).

contentId.description: Content-node id, used to build download hrefs for legacy (non-file_id) attachments.

placeholder.description: Passes through to the spotlight trigger's label. Non-string values are left undefined (SearchSpotlightTrigger's own fallback applies).

showAvatar.description: Show the member's photo beside their name; off centres name+profession under the quote.

textTheme.description: See shared:textTheme. The quote's ink — the quote text, the attribution name, and the role all take the resolved colour. Unset = Auto (the surrounding section surface's own ink, per the MIO-492 auto-contrast / `surface.ink`, exactly as without the key). The attribution role stays a derived muted opacity of the resolved colour (mirrors the unset-state relationship between the quote text and the role, not a separate independently-set tone).

sticky.description: Pins the bar to the top of the viewport for the whole page (MIO-2734). `reveal:"after-scroll"` forces sticky on regardless of this flag.

tone.description: Drives the notice-bar tint AND the ARIA role (alert/status).

appearance.description: 'page' is the DS nav-bar frosted-chrome surface (page bg + blur), tone-independent — used by the scroll-revealed action bar, not the tint/solid urgency-bar family.

justify.description: 'between' is the DS nav-bar row shape (logo left / CTA right).

contentWidth.description: 'content' caps the row to max-w-hub-content + the section gutter, landing its edges at the same x position as the page's content column — the surface itself stays full-bleed.

reveal.description: 'after-scroll' hides the bar until the page scrolls past the first viewport, forces sticky on, and paints at a lower z-index than an urgency banner above it.

title.description: Deadline sentence override. Omit to auto-format from `value` (an ISO date string), locale+timezone aware.

expiredLabel.description: Sentence shown once the deadline in `value` has passed.

ctaLabel.description: Built-in CTA label — only rendered when `size:'small'`.

ctaAction.description: Same Action pipeline as `button.action` — paired with `ctaLabel`.

size.description: Doubles as the layout switch (cell strip vs deadline-sentence block).

hideOnExpire.description: Hide the whole widget once expired, instead of swapping to `expiredLabel`.

height.description: 'normal'=24px chrome-scale, 'lg'=40px (28px mobile) mid-scale, 'hero'=71px (48px mobile) content-scale. ALSO accepts an absolute px NUMBER (MIO-3227/MIO-3335) — freeform:true admits any number here; the renderer (logo.tsx, LOGO_HEIGHT_PX_MIN/MAX) clamps it to [16,320] and applies it via inline `style.height` at every breakpoint (deliberately non-responsive, unlike the enum steps), falling back to 'normal' outside that range or for any other unrecognized value.

src.description: Per-node logo asset override. Absolute http(s) or same-origin-relative URL, validated same as isValidImageUrl (node-surface.tsx). An invalid or unset value falls back to the hub's own branding logo_url.

label.description: aria-label on the radiogroup wrapping the plan-card children.

defaultSelected.description: Seeds selection when this is the first such child in a plan-group (or seeds the standalone local toggle when rendered outside one). Content (name/price/currency/period/description/badge/save) lives on `value`, not settings — outside the settings-vocabulary contract, same precedent as kind:quote.

groupId.description: Required. Id of the plan-group node this leaf subscribes to. Resolved contextually, not just literally: when no plan-group is registered under this exact id but exactly one group is registered on the page, that sole group is used instead; with zero or 2+ candidate groups, no link is made and `fallback` renders.

fallback.description: Rendered for SSR/first paint and whenever `groupId` has never published a selection. Must byte-match the subscribed group's `defaultSelected` card's own `price`/`period` — no reformatting happens in the pub-sub relay.

size.description: Each step bakes in its own mobile value at the hub 659px breakpoint (sm 40→23, md 56→33, lg 81→47, xl 110→64).

rotate.description: Named values (90|180|270) resolve to static Tailwind rotate classes; any other numeric value falls back to an inline style.rotate.

drawDelay.description: Extra delay (seconds) on top of the viewport trigger — used to chain a second doodle so it visibly waits for a first one to finish drawing.

hideOnMobile.description: Literal @max-[659px]/hub:hidden — scoped to this leaf, not a general leaf capability.

icon.description: Hub sprite glyph name. Optional when `label` is given.

label.description: Short text (e.g. a step numeral). Wins over `icon` when both are set.

variant.description: 'outline' (hollow disc, rides ambient currentColor) is the journey-stage marker treatment.

size.description: 72/88/104px, steps down one tier at max-sm.

draw.description: Pen-draw a single stroked glyph on mount — a CSS-keyframe mechanism, distinct from doodle.draw (Motion, viewport-triggered).

documents.title: Add your first lesson
documents.description:
This is a placeholder lesson — open it in the editor and swap it for your first real one.

## Three ways to add content

- **Upload a video or audio file** — drop it in and it becomes the lesson media.
- **Attach a document** — add a worksheet, PDF, or slide deck members can download.
- **Write a text lesson** — skip the upload and write directly in the editor.

## Title and description matter

The title is what members see on the card and at the top of the lesson. The description does double duty: it's the short blurb under the card, and for text lessons, it's the lesson body itself — so write it like you mean it. Once you're happy with it, do the same for the other two placeholder lessons in this playlist.

documents.title: Add another lesson
documents.description:
Every lesson members open is built from three simple parts you control from here.

## What members see

- **Overview** — the lesson content itself: your uploaded video or audio, or the text you write directly in the editor.
- **Attachments** — worksheets, slide decks, or any file you want members to download alongside the lesson.
- **Comments** — a space under the lesson where members can ask questions or talk about what they just went through.

## Keeping track

Members can mark a lesson complete once they've finished it, and that progress carries forward through the rest of the playlist. You don't need to fill in every part on day one — Attachments and Comments are there when you need them, and an empty Overview just means there's no content uploaded yet.

documents.title: Add another lesson
documents.description:
This lesson lives inside a playlist, and how you order things here shapes how members move through it.

## Order sets the pace

Lessons play in the order you arrange them in this playlist — put your strongest opener first, and each one carries momentum into the next.

## What members see as they go

- **Progress** — the hub tracks how far each member has gotten, so they can pick up right where they left off.
- **Durations and read times** — every card shows how long a video runs or how long a text lesson takes to read, so members know what they're signing up for before they click.
- **Prev / next** — the watch page carries simple controls to move to the next lesson in the playlist without going back to the list.

Reorder lessons any time from the editor — nothing here is locked in.
